subject: Mutual Action Plan: NutrifyLabs POC — roles, benchmarks, and timelines
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan@nutrifylabs.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: NutrifyLabs POC — roles, benchmarks, and timelines

Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, I’m kicking off the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the NutrifyLabs POC so we have a single doc for success criteria, owners, and a realistic close timeline. I attached a first-pass MAP and a concise benchmark plan.

High-level POC summary (4 weeks):
- Week 0: dataset handoff + infra prep
- Week 1: base model integration + prompt sweep
- Week 2: benchmark runs (latency, throughput, accuracy)
- Week 3: iteration window + final assessment + executive review

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 200ms for 64-token requests under typical traffic (see benchmark-plan.md)
- Cost: target inference cost < $0.75 per 1k tokens at P95 after batching optimizations
- Quality: semantic-search embedding MAP@5 improvement >= 8% vs current baseline on Nutrify validation set
- Stability: no unplanned errors > 0.5% of requests during sustained 5-min window at target load

Suggested owners (Redwood):
- Aisha Rahman — Account lead / overall MAP coordinator
- Rafael Mendes — Solutions & prompt engineering lead
- Grace O'Connor — Evaluation and metrics owner (prompt sets, eval harness)
- Marcus Lin — Dedicated infra & test instance owner

Suggested owners (NutrifyLabs):
- Jordan Hayes — Product lead / sign-off on success criteria
- Priya Desai — Data science lead (dataset and labeling questions)
- Procurement contact (procurement@nutrifylabs.com) — contracting & commercial

Immediate asks:
1) Confirm the success criteria above or propose edits by EOD Thu (14 May).
2) Confirm primary POC contact(s) on the Nutrify side for dataset handoff and access (S3 or secure share).
3) Pick a 45-minute kickoff slot next week (I’ve proposed calendar options in the MAP workbook).

Attachments: Nutrify_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), benchmark-plan.md (benchmark test plan), sample-dataset-schema.csv (expected schema).

Thanks — excited to get this rolling.

—
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
<aisha_rahman@redwood.com> | +1 415-555-0139

-- attachment stubs: Nutrify_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx), benchmark-plan.md (text)

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: NutrifyLabs POC — roles, benchmarks, and timelines

Aisha — appreciate the clear plan and heads-up. Confirming NutrifyLabs is good to move forward. A few notes inline: 

- Timeline: 4 weeks sounds fine but can we add a "buffer week" for legal/contract signoff if needed (we typically need an extra week for procurement).
- Success criteria: the quality target (MAP@5 +8%) is reasonable; Priya and I would like to add an operational metric: end-to-end request success rate >= 99.5% during bench runs. Can Redwood include request tracing so we can map any failed cases to request IDs?
- Dataset: Priya will own the dataset handoff. We will share a sanitized 50k record sample by Thu (14 May). We will upload to an S3 bucket and share short-term credentials.

Owners on our side: Jordan Hayes (PM, POC sign-off), Priya Desai (Data science lead), Michael Evans (Infra lead — cc'd later for access). Procurement will engage if contract changes are required.

Proposed kickoff: Thu 14 May 10:00–10:45 PT — does that work for Redwood?

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: NutrifyLabs POC — roles, benchmarks, and timelines

Looping in to confirm internal owners and a concrete plan for prompts/evals. Quick notes from the engineering side: 

1) Prompt & eval ownership:
- Grace will curate the initial prompt set (50 canonical prompts + 200 edge cases) and own the eval harness (automated scoring + manual spot checks).
- I will run the first round of prompt tuning and provide a config file with recommended system prompts and temperature schedules.

2) Benchmark & tooling:
- Marcus will provision a dedicated dev instance (GPU pool) for the POC and a separate load-test cluster for throughput runs.
- We will include detailed tracing (request ID) and token-level latency breakdowns in the benchmark outputs. That should satisfy the request-tracing ask.

3) Timeline adjustments:
- We recommend keeping the 4-week technical plan but explicitly include an optional "contract buffer week" between Week 0 and Week 1 for procurement. I'll mark that in the MAP workbook.

4) Data handling:
- Priya: thanks in advance for the sample. Please confirm the S3 location and whether the sample contains any PII — we will treat the upload as potentially sensitive and can support a signed-off NDAs if needed.

Next steps I will take today: update MAP workbook with prompt & eval owner columns, drop an initial prompt list into the Drive folder, and create a basic Jenkins job for scheduled benchmark runs.

—
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0192
